comparisons.peer_topic: UK CMA Sovereign Bond Antitrust Settlement
comparisons.peer_summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed a £17.16 million fine on Citigroup and CGML for unlawfully sharing information regarding British pound sterling-denominated government bonds, resolving conduct that occurred between 2011 and 2013.
comparisons.comparison: Both Morgan Stanley and Citigroup disclose recent settlements with the U.K. Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) regarding anti-competitive arrangements in fixed income products during the same timeframe. Morgan Stanley settled on February 21, 2025, concerning liquid fixed income products between 2009 and 2012, while Citigroup also settled with the CMA on February 21, 2025, regarding British pound sterling-denominated government bonds (gilts) between 2011 and 2013, resulting in a £17.16 million fine for Citigroup. Both disclosures identify the CMA as the regulator and the settlement date as February 21, 2025, indicating a coordinated industry resolution to similar investigations.

sentences.text: On February 21, 2025, the U.K. Competition and Markets Authority announced a settlement with the Firm, as well as other financial institutions, in connection with its investigation of suspected anti-competitive arrangements in the financial services sector, specifically regarding the Firm's activities concerning certain liquid fixed income products between 2009 and 2012.

Regulatory Action: On May 24, 2023, the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) announced that it had provisionally found that Citigroup, CGML, and four other banks unlawfully shared information related to the buying and selling of British pound sterling-denominated government bonds issued by the United Kingdom.
On February 21, 2025, the CMA announced resolutions with Citigroup and CGML related to conduct that occurred between 2011 and 2013 and imposed a fine of £17.16 million.
